name: Wunderdog Sports
title: Wunderdog Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Is It Worth It?
description: Wunderdog review, checked 7 Nov 2026: prices from $15 to $5,499, how the free package guarantee works, what its public pick log shows, and what buyers say.
dek: A one man pick service run by Geoff, who calls himself the Wunderdog, selling since 2001. Packages run from $15 to $5,499 a year, a losing package earns a free replacement package rather than cash, and the site posts a long pick log that it keeps itself. Its own totals show small profits at about 52% to 53% winners.

status.label: Not verified
status.note: Watchdog has not graded a full, time stamped record for Wunderdog. Its pick archive is published and graded by Wunderdog itself. This page reports what we could check and labels everything else.

glance: Wunderdog Sports Picks LLC, terms governed by Colorado law; phone 877-DOG WINS (terms and support pages)
$15 office pool week to $5,499 for all sports for one year
Free equivalent package if a package ends with a net unit loss. No cash refunds once delivered
A pick archive with prices and results, kept by the seller
short_answer: Wunderdog is a real, long running business. It names a company, Wunderdog Sports Picks LLC, publishes its prices, lists a phone line and email, and sells one person's picks. In that narrow sense it is legitimate.

It also does something most pick sellers do not: it posts an archive of past Pro Picks with the line, the price, the units, the result and the time each pick was released. The totals it shows are modest, such as NFL 3253-2897 (53%) for +195.3 units over 25.1 years. That archive is kept and graded by Wunderdog, not by an outside party, so we could not confirm it is complete.

Its guarantee replaces a losing package with another one free. It never returns cash, and the terms say there are no refunds once a product is delivered. If you buy, buy short, log every pick yourself with the price you actually got, and remember that even the seller's own long run numbers sit just above break even.

guarantee: The guarantee page says that if the picks do not "result in a profit for you (more units won than lost based on recommended unit plays)" over the package, you receive an equivalent package for free. In a combo, each sport is judged separately. Horse racing picks carry no guarantee. The product listings describe the same rule: an equivalent package sent automatically if the package does not show positive net units.

This is a replacement, not a refund. The terms page says "Once a product has been delivered, there are no refunds," and that no part of the fee is refunded on termination. The guarantee is measured in Wunderdog's own units at its recommended sizes and prices, so a buyer who bets different amounts or gets worse lines can lose money while the package counts as a win. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered, and those are usually far larger than the package price.

One more detail in the terms: they describe the subscription fee as a "capital contribution" to a Wunderdog Sports Trust, paid in exchange for access to digital services, with no equity or financial return. The terms do not explain why they are written this way. A buyer should simply understand that the terms promise picks, not money back.

claims_note: We searched for the Harvard Business Review case study and did not find one. We did find a 3 page case called "Wunderdog Sports Picks" published on 8 Apr 2008 by the Darden School of Business at the University of Virginia, used in a statistics course. Its listing says the case is little more than an email to a professor claiming 87 of 149 correct NFL picks against the spread in 2005, and asks students to judge what that record shows. That is a teaching exercise about evaluating a claim, not an endorsement of the picks.

Some numbers do not line up from page to page. The homepage says 85,000+ documented picks and the about page says 88,334. The all sports one year package is labeled "just $2 per pick" while its description says "about $1.00 per pick." The about page says over 25 years in business and over 30 years betting, while a homepage video blurb says three decades in the industry. None of this proves anything about the picks, but the marketing is not kept consistent.
To its credit, the long run totals Wunderdog advertises are modest and close to break even, not the 70% claims common in this business. Its about page says outright that no one hits 60% long term.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing we could find. We found no full, time stamped log kept by a third party, no contest results run by an outside organizer that we opened, and no regulator or court record. The awards on the about page were not checked.

What Wunderdog itself publishes: sport archive pages list past Pro Picks back to 2001 for the NFL, with game, date, kickoff time, units, line and price, and the past pick page we opened showed the release time and a graded result. For example, a 2 unit pick on Miami +5 (-110) for 25 Oct 2026 was shown as released to clients on 23 Oct 2026 at 12:12PM ET and graded a win. That is far more than most pick sellers show. But the archive is kept and graded by the seller, and we could not confirm that no pick is missing or changed.

What the seller's own numbers say: NFL 3,253 wins and 2,897 losses for +195.3 units works out to about 0.03 units of profit per decided pick over 25 years. If those numbers are complete and accurate, they describe a small edge with long losing stretches, not a fast way to make money. A buyer who pays for picks and gets worse prices than the posted lines could easily end up behind.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition Wunderdog is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how its picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: Wunderdog's own NFL archive shows 53% winners over 25 years. On the Watchdog board on 7 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Wunderdog is thin. The Trustpilot page we opened had 10 reviews, split between praise and complaints, and the testimonials on Wunderdog's own site are chosen by Wunderdog. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: Buyer reports on forums are few and old. A Sportsbook Review member said in 2009 that a season pass he bought had been solid, winning over 60 percent. A 2020 thread opened with someone whose first three free picks all lost, and the one reply called the service legitimate but a long term proposition. We found no recent buyer posting a full season result.

Wunderdog runs a testimonials page and quotes customer notes on its homepage and guarantee page, including buyers who praise its honesty and the free replacement package. These are selected and published by the seller, so they cannot tell you what a typical buyer experiences.
Trustpilot showed a TrustScore of 3.6 from 10 reviews on a profile claimed by the company: six 5 star and four 1 star reviews, with company replies to the negative ones. Ten reviews is not a sample.
A reviewer who described himself as a long time customer praised the detailed analysis and said staff were helpful and quick to respond.

A reviewer reported heavy losses on a multi sport subscription, said a refund was refused and questioned the unit sizing. Wunderdog replied, disputed the size of the loss from the figures given and asked the reviewer to email for an account review.

A reviewer said a Game of the Month pick lost, the free replacement package started automatically, and he still finished down overall. He criticized the guarantee. Wunderdog's reply explained the automatic replacement, acknowledged he was down overall and offered a free package.
A reviewer said recent picks had done poorly and that the guarantee does not return the money spent.
A reviewer called the service trustworthy and said a technical glitch was fixed quickly, with a bonus pick offered.
A Better Business Bureau search for Wunderdog returned no business profile. We found no Reddit thread and no TheRX, Covers or SBR forum thread with a substantial discussion of the service.

conflicts: The support page says each Pro Pick includes "a link to the sportsbook where I found the best line." We could not see those links without buying, so we do not know whether they are affiliate links that pay Wunderdog. We saw no sportsbook promo codes or revenue share links on the public pages we opened.
The terms say the site uses third party advertising companies to serve ads. We found no parent company or sportsbook ownership tie.
strengths: A public archive of past Pro Picks going back years, with line, price, units, release time and result on each pick page. Few pick sellers show this much.
Advertised long run results are modest, about 52% to 53%, and the about page openly warns that no one hits 60% long term.
Prices and the guarantee rule are written out, free picks and a daily email let a reader see the style before buying, and the company replies to negative reviews.
concerns: The pick archive is kept and graded by the seller. No outside party confirms it is complete.
The guarantee gives another package, never cash, and the terms say there are no refunds once a product is delivered. Betting losses are never covered.
Even taken at face value, the seller's long run totals show a thin edge that worse prices could erase.
Marketing numbers change between pages, and the Harvard Business Review case study claim did not match what we could find.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: It is a real business, Wunderdog Sports Picks LLC, selling picks since 2001 with published prices and a public archive of past picks. We could not independently verify that its picks win over time, because that archive is kept and graded by Wunderdog itself.

On 7 Nov 2026 single day packages cost $25 to $40, weekly packages $125 to $204, monthly packages $299 to $499, and single sport seasons $549 to $1,499. The all sports one year package cost $5,499, and NFL office pool picks cost $15 a week.
Does Wunderdog have a verified record?

Not independently. Wunderdog posts a long pick archive with lines, prices, release times and results, which is more than most sellers show, but no outside party keeps or audits it, and no Watchdog graded record is matched to Wunderdog.

For the money you get one handicapper's picks with written analysis, unit sizes and the line at release, plus a free package if a package ends with a unit loss. What is unproven is whether the seller's own small long run edge, about 53% in the NFL, holds up for a buyer who cannot always get the posted price, and the guarantee never returns cash.
